segments.text: Thank you, Mr. Chairman, ladies and gentlemen.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As introduced, I'm Dr. Peter McCullough from Dallas, Texas.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I'm in clinical practice.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I've seen and examined hundreds of patients with acute COVID-19.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I've advised on many more hundreds, and now I'm seeing and examining patients who are incurring fatal and non-fatal injuries from the COVID-19 vaccine program.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I presented to the U.S. Senate November 19, 2020, an outline of how our governments
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: at the federal and state level should be comprehensively responding to the pandemic.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And I subsequently published that in December of 2020 in the peer-reviewed literature.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And as Senator Mastriano has stated, there are four pillars to pandemic response.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There is a comprehensive way
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: to address a widespread viral illness that leads to hospitalization and death.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The first pillar is to reduce the spread of the virus.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As each person becomes ill with the syndrome, they can indeed pass it to a susceptible person.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But transmission is only from acutely ill to susceptible person, only.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Only that has now been sufficiently shown in the peer-reviewed literature.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Someone who has no symptoms poses no threat to someone else, whether they be susceptible or not susceptible.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That means on pillar number one, there should have never been any lockdowns.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There should never have been any social distancing or any measures for people who are well.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That means that the Great Barrington Declaration that was proposed by Dr. J. Bhattacharya from Stanford, Martin Kolda from Harvard, and Suneetra Gupta from Oxford, that indeed they were correct that the only thing we should have done with respect to reducing the spread of the virus is to protect
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: the vulnerable, and that is the very elderly, since we learned early that risk stratification was possible.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The infection does not affect people equally.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: For a 10-year-old child, it's typically less than a common cold.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But for a 90-year-old person, it can be a fatal illness.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Age is a tremendous risk stratifier.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is terribly important because our methods of reducing the spread of the illness
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: should have always been placed on those who are acutely ill with quarantining for the acutely ill. That was the method to reduce the spread of the virus.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We subsequently learned, to be fair, not right away, that oral and nasal virucidal treatment
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That is actually killing the virus in the nasopharynx with dilute hydrogen peroxide or dilute Pavadone iodine is far and away the most effective way to reduce the contagiousness of someone who has the virus.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Far more contagious.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Sadly, masks, hand sanitizers, social distancing, all have been subject to study and all of them have failed.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Pillar number two is early treatment.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Early treatment also reduces the spread of the illness because untreated, the average person is contagious and spreads the illness for two weeks.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But early treatment, using a variety of drugs, reduces the spread of the illness, reduces the duration of infectivity to about three to four days.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That is a massive difference.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Anybody can stay at home sick for three or four days.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Very hard for someone to stay quarantined for 14 days.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: To make matters worse, with no early treatment, individuals who do progress and become progressively ill
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: They get to some panic phase of the illness, and either start making urgent care trips, spreading the virus more, or calling family members, or paramedics, or Uber drivers, or taxi drivers, and further spreading the illness.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So early treatment also works to spread the spread of the illness.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And early treatment using a variety of drugs, and what's called sequence multi-drug therapy for COVID-19, reduces the risks of hospitalization and death with the full breadth of drugs that we have right now by 95%.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There are drugs that reduce viral replication, including now an EUA approved drug by Pfizer, another one by Merck, which should be featured and used.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We have monoclonal antibodies, which are products of Operation Warp Speed, which I've used consistently in my practice in high-risk patients, which are safe and effective.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We use cortical steroids, other anti-inflammatories, and blood thinners, which should not be controversial.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: I presented this on the U.S. Senate floor November 19th of 2020, and I told the Senate, I told America, it should not be controversial.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Whether I prescribe prednisone for an asthmatic patient or for a patient with acute COVID-19,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There should be absolutely no resistance.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There should be no reluctance and there certainly shouldn't be any type of chill put on an attempt for a doctor to treat an acutely sick patient.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: As we sit here today, my estimates are 95% of Americans who have died of COVID-19 and we're approaching nearly a million of these poor souls and tens of millions of hospitalizations could have been avoided with a comprehensive early treatment approach.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And to this day, we've gone through two presidential administrations, two surgeon generals, two White House task force, CDC leadership, NIH and FDA, not a single leader at the federal level has said that there are two bad outcomes of COVID-19, hospitalization and death, and we are gonna make an effort.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: We are gonna bring the best and brightest doctors together and stop these hospitalizations and deaths.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: To this day, that hasn't been done.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Pillar number three, in-hospital care.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: in hospital care is a last resort.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: No one should be thinking that the eventuality is hospitalization, but in fact it's occurred.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It's occurred tens of millions of times.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The vast majority of deaths with COVID-19 occur in hospitalized patients.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Meaning we have two weeks, three weeks, four weeks of time to try to treat this illness before the patient dies on week five.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: In the NIH autopsy study, the very first autopsy study published by Chertow and colleagues of individuals who died and courageously the doctors did autopsies, the average person had nine days at home and no mention of early treatment before they go in the hospital and the treatment is applied too late.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Now, there are a bevy of treatments that can be done in the hospital.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It's largely supportive care.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But I want to make the observation, I want to make the record known, not a single hospital in the United States and not a single hospital in this state claims to be a center of excellence for the treatment of COVID-19.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Now we're two years into this.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: These same centers, and you have them in this great state, claim to be experts of centers of excellence in cancer care and cardiovascular care.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Yet COVID-19 has been a large book of business for hospitalized patients, and there appears to be no claim of excellence.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There have been no attempts for comparative effectiveness
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: of who's doing better in the hospital and why.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There is no presentation of best practices in hospital care so hospitals can learn and start to save more American lives.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: No mention.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: No mention.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And I think each and every lawmaker should look in their constituents and talk to the health systems and say, what in the world are you doing with inpatient COVID-19?
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Tell me how good you are and let's see your outcomes.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Let's see more Americans who do get hospitalized walk home as opposed to end up in the morgue.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: This is astonishing that not a single hospital in the United States claims to be a center of excellence.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Not a single hospital is actively recruiting patients who are acutely sick so they can save them.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Not a single one.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Pillar number four.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Pillar number four is vaccination.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That vaccination could play a role in reducing the burden of COVID-19.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And it has always been reasonable, as the Great Barrington Declaration stated, to have a vaccine for our high-risk seniors and those working in domicile facilities.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That's about 2.7 million Americans probably should have received a vaccine if a vaccine would have been safe and effective.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That's it.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: That is it.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Nursing homes are the only place where there was documented healthcare worker to patient spread.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The only place.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The only place, there was never any documented hospital healthcare worker to patient spread or vice versa in the United States.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There were no major school outbreaks in the United States.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There was never a documented case of a student to teacher transmission with serious outcomes.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: yet quickly after the vaccine program rolled out, there was very little attention placed on our seniors.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The average age of someone dying with COVID-19 is deep into the 80s.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: A large fraction of the deaths are nursing home residents.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There seems to be no interest in nursing home residents.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: There seems to be a progressive interest in vaccinating younger and younger individuals who are not at risk for severe outcomes.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And as evidence of that, in a paper by Borah Willa and colleagues from the New York State database, they have data now on 1.1 million children who have received the COVID-19 vaccine in the last few months.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And they found in each strata a few hundred out of 1.1 million who, in fact, were hospitalized.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: None of the children died.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The calculated vaccine efficacy of any of the vaccines applied in children was less than 20%.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: A minimally acceptable standard for a vaccine for any human being to consider is a vaccine efficacy validly and fairly calculated at 50%.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Anything below half is not worth doing.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And to make matters worse, the CDC is published by Anne House in the December 31st issue of the MMWR, a paper titled COVID-19 Vaccine Safety in Children Aged 5 to 11 in the United States.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: and what and house and her colleagues from the cdc found is that uh... among four thousand two hundred and forty nine individuals who received uh... vaccine these young children twenty seven point uh... uh... i'm sorry sixty uh... four percent bc had some type of adverse effect twenty seven point nine percent had no adverse effect and in this group the most concerning thing to me as a cardiologist of the hundred cases
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: that were severe.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Now, one case would be too many.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: One case, because children of this age group do not have severe outcomes, these children who were subjected to the vaccine, 100 of them had severe outcomes, and among those, 15% had evidence of heart injury, ages 5 to 11.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And it gets worse in ages, the reactions reported by the parents.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So what I just gave you was reported to the CDC by doctors and nurses and others.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: What the parents report through what's called the v-safe system, which they can report on their cell phone,
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: that on dose number one, 34.7% of children had a systemic reaction.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: 40.9% had, it was on dose one, 40.9% on dose two.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The parents report 10.9% and 15.1% respectively had a health impact on the child's life for taking the vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So as we sit here today, if the topic of discussion is childhood vaccination, it is clear, based on publications of representative data, that the risks far outweigh any potential benefits of vaccinating children.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: and the data are clear.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And in the last few weeks now, reports have come in, one from Connecticut with oversight from the pathology from the University of Michigan and from the University of Minnesota on two teenage boys who died on days three and four after the Pfizer vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: And the parents were horrified to find the children dead at home.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: autopsies were performed and the conclusion was crystal clear, the vaccines caused the death with massive heart inflammation and evidence of superimposed catecholamine injury on the heart.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Fatal reports have come in from Choi and from Verma, Choi in Korea, Verma from Washington University in St. Louis.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It is clear that a vaccine is being
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: pushed is being encouraged and mandating that in fact results in death of children.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Results in death of children.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: One death is too many as I've shared with you in millions of children receiving the vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: They don't die of COVID-19 respiratory illness.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: But in fact, they die of the vaccine.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: So the proponents of the data suggest now with the Omicron variant and beyond, the vaccines have out mutated the ability.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: The virus has out mutated the ability of the vaccines to cover them.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: All experts agree the vaccines do not last six months.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: All the vaccine manufacturers agree that they have to make new vaccines to cover new variants.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: It's my viewpoint as a physician and as a public citizen.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: that all vaccine mandates should immediately be dropped and all current vaccines be pulled from the market and undergo a very intensive review on safety and efficacy and figure out where the vaccine program has gone wrong.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Those are my comments.
segments.speaker: SPEAKER_00

segments.text: Thank you.
